Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 45311 of 2024

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Madan Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
As informed by learned AGA, notice to the informant has been served on 03.12.2024 but none is present on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Madan Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ashwani Kumar Tripathi,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 62 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) of I.P.C. and Sections 5L/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Katghar, District - Moradabad, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by 24 days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
There is no medical evidence to corroborate the prosecution story.

Chhotu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88740856/
1 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel has also argued that the victim is the consenting party as is evident from her statement recorded u/s 183 BNSS.
There is no clinching evidence to suggest that the applicant misled the victim from the beginning.
The informant has converted a failed consensual physical relationship into a criminal case.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.03.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. The Supreme Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another, 2019 (9)
SCC 608 and Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 886, has stated that entering into any kind of corporeal relationship with a person on the false promise to marry cannot be termed as rape.

entities.text:
Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another, 2019 (9)
SCC 608
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 886
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. This Court has avoided expressing its opinion as the case hinges on whether the applicant's promise of marriage was genuine or false and whether the physical relationship was consensual or not.
It is for the Trial Court to draw a conclusion which will depend on the evidence presented before it and its interpretation as per law.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant- Chhotu, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Chhotu vs State Of U.P.
